evidence: app/package.json:17 — nitro pinned to exact pre-release '3.0.260610-beta' (date-coded ≈2026-06-10); nitro v3 is still pre-stable (README on registry.npmjs.org/nitro: 'For the current stable release, see Nitro v2'; v3.0.261029-rc published 2026-10-29)
app/package.json:8 — 'start': 'node .output/server/index.mjs' — the beta is load-bearing as the production server
app/vite.config.ts:8 — nitro() is the production build plugin, so the beta governs both build and runtime
app/package.json:14 — '@solidjs/start': '^2.1.0' — framework stable only since 2026-08-04; the pinned minor shipped 2026-10-22, and it is central to all 14 source files
app/package.json:16 — 'vite': '^8.3.5' — Vite 8 stable since 2026-03-12, a required peer of @solidjs/start
reach.rationale: Exactly one pre-release dependency (nitro v3 beta) in a load-bearing role, plus the whole app riding a recently-stable framework major whose stable release is ~3 months old — that matches the 'one or two / recently-stable in central places' anchor, not 'several central features on experimental'.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:6-9 — the entire nitro footprint is a single bare plugin call with zero nitro-specific options
app/package.json:17 — plus the version pin; the only other touchpoint is the start script at package.json:8
app/src/ (grep 'unstable|experimental|islands|clientOnly|preload|cache(') — zero nitro imports or experimental names anywhere in the 14 source files
app/vite.config.ts:7 — solidStart() also takes no options, so no experimental flags to unwind
containment.rationale: The one experimental dependency is confined to the build config and package manifest with no options and no imports in application code; swapping or upgrading it is a two-file change, which is as contained as it gets.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:8 — nitro() after solidStart() is the exact recipe in docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/guides/deployment-plugins ('Add nitro() after solidStart()'); nitro v3 is the only portable Node-server deployment plugin for SolidStart 2 (the v1 nitro-2 path is deprecated per the migration guide)
app/src/lib/queries.ts:348,514 — 'use server' placed inside each query per the v2 reference docs, the documented stable pattern rather than a novel one
app/vite.config.ts:6-9 — restraint: no experimental.tasks, no islands, no ssr:'data-only' (the newest 2.1.0 feature), despite being on the newest minor
app/package.json:16 — vite@8 is a required peer (vite ^8 || ^9) of the chosen framework, not a gratuitous reach
justification.rationale: Nitro v3 is mandated by SolidStart 2's current stable release and is the only supported way to get a plain-Node production server, so nothing a stable alternative could provide is being passed up; nothing in the source reaches for new APIs for novelty.

findings.issue: nitro is pinned to an exact pre-release beta (3.0.260610-beta, ≈June 2026) that is already stale — nitro v3 shipped 3.0.261029-rc on 2026-10-29 with a documented beta→RC breaking-changes list, so the app is frozen on an abandoned point of the channel while the runtime contract keeps moving.
findings.suggestion: Track the channel (e.g. '^3.0.260610-beta' or bump to the current RC once SolidStart's docs bless it) and rely on package-lock.json for reproducibility; since usage is confined to vite.config.ts, verify a bump by re-running the build + start once.

findings.issue: 'start': 'node .output/server/index.mjs' couples the app to nitro v3's internal output layout; a beta-to-RC upgrade that changes the entry path would break npm start silently.
findings.suggestion: Note the nitro upgrade path in README.md and re-check the start script (or use the nitro-provided start/preview CLI) whenever the pin is bumped.

findings.issue: @solidjs/start@^2.1.0 is a caret range over a framework whose stable major is only ~3 months old and whose pinned minor is 8 days old, so each fresh install can pick up a newer, less-battle-tested minor than the one tested.
findings.suggestion: Keep the caret but build with 'npm ci' from the committed package-lock.json in CI/harness so production builds are reproducible until the framework matures.

findings.issue: vite and nitro are listed as runtime 'dependencies' rather than devDependencies, though both are build-time tools.
findings.suggestion: Harmless and consistent with the official migration guide ('npm i … vite@8', 'npm i nitro'), so leaving as-is is fine; moving them to devDependencies would just be conventional hygiene if the lockfile ever gets regenerated.

summary: The application code itself contains zero experimental APIs — every import is a long-stable or fully documented SolidStart v2 pattern, and vite.config.ts sets no experimental flags. The only pre-release element is the dependency stack: an exact-pinned nitro v3 beta that serves as both the production server and build plugin, beneath a framework stable for just ~3 months. That reach is justified and well-contained — nitro v3 is the only portable Node-server deployment plugin SolidStart 2's docs prescribe, and its footprint is two files — leaving the stale, exactly-pinned beta as the one genuine maintenance risk.
